title: HVOF Tungsten Carbide Coating of the Main Landing Gear Sliding Tube in Place of Hard Chrome Plating

ata.title: Main Gear — Main Gear Leg Assembly

abstract: The chromium electroplated running surface of the main landing gear sliding tube is replaced by a high velocity oxygen fuel sprayed tungsten carbide coating, removing a hexavalent chromium process from the overhaul chain and doubling the overhaul interval.

sections.reason: Hard chrome plating of landing gear running surfaces relies on hexavalent chromium, whose industrial authorisation is being withdrawn across the supply chain. Two of the four approved overhaul shops had already given notice that they would stop offering the process, which would have left the fleet dependent on a single plant for a component with a twelve-year overhaul cycle. The change was launched on obsolescence grounds, but the coating also lasts appreciably longer in service, so the case was made on both counts.
sections.description: The chromium electroplated running surface of the sliding tube is replaced by a high velocity oxygen fuel sprayed tungsten carbide cobalt chromium coating, ground and superfinished to the same diameter and surface roughness as the plated surface so that no seal change is required. The clamp D3210114090552 at the torque link is renewed because the coating build-up alters the clearance, the vendor clamp CAD561133-34 is retained, and the obsolete sensor kit D3210110015901 is deleted from the leg assembly. The gear leg FINs 2002GM and 330GB are unchanged; the main gear sensor FIN 1545GM keeps its position. Work is done at overhaul with the leg removed from the aircraft, and the aircraft-level activity is limited to the leg change from zones 721, 732 and 734. Drawings D32101129334 issue A and D32101164484 issue C carry the coating specification and the grinding tolerances.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 1.4 kg per leg, symmetric, with no measurable balance effect. No electrical load change. The coated tube is fully interchangeable with the plated tube at leg level; the two may be mixed across the two legs of one aircraft. Scoring resistance measured on the trial legs was roughly three times better, and the sliding tube overhaul interval moves from six to twelve years. AMM and IPC content for ATA 32-10 will be re-issued to reflect the deleted sensor kit, and the component maintenance manual is being rewritten.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z09673 in August 2018. In service the change is embodied at the next scheduled leg overhaul rather than as a campaign, which is why the bulletin is written as an overhaul-shop instruction and carries no aircraft downtime beyond the normal leg change.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric mass reduction, no measurable CG effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z09673; two overhaul shops requalified before cut-in
